(b) A pure core/rule-fidelity.ts lists a rule's SPECIFICS: HTTP status codes and classes (400, 4xx), paths (a token with `/` between word characters, or a file name with an extension), and values (backticked spans, double-quoted spans, tokens carrying a digit). It then reports the specifics the quote lacks, by case-insensitive whitespace-collapsed substring. (c) Standing constraints renders each quoted rule as `- [D<n>] <rule> — operator: "<quote>"`, plus ` (not in the operator's words: <specifics>)` when any are missing. (d) sofar_log_decision returns `warnings[]`, and `sofar event append --type decision_logged` prints them, naming the unquoted specifics; never a refusal. (e) The `rule` and `quote` descriptions and the CLI dialect's fields teach: word the rule as the operator did, and pass their words as quote.
